comments.author: hangsi
comments.story: Senate passes reauthorization of key US surveillance program after midnight
comments.why: Fictional surveillance tech that is plausible today
comments.text: "Beautiful. Unethical. Dangerous." So says Morgan Freeman's character Lucius Fox in 2008 in The Dark Knight[0]. The rest of the tech imagined in that scene is plausible today too, considering the density of WiFi/5G and research demonstrating the potential for its use as passive radar [1]. That paper metions a cooperative base station, but I am wondering if there is any value gained in knowing exactly what the traffic is (such as some of the intelligence community does) in modelling how the waves propagate and performing an even more passive observation. [0] [VIDEO] [1] Samczyński et al. 2021 [LINK]

comments.author: netsharc
comments.why: Film scene of sonar-based surveillance as an analogy
comments.text: Like Deja Vu ( [LINK] ), The Dark Knight's sonar ( [VIDEO] ) or the series Devs. I've always thought it'd be amazing to be able to view an event from different angles via crowd-sourced videos, and that it was very doable. From an information scientist point of view, I'm glad to see it's been done.
